   136→// NormalizeAfterLoad applies backward-compatible migrations to state loaded from disk.
   137→// Call this after deserializing a State from JSON.
   138→func (s *State) NormalizeAfterLoad() {
   139→	// Migrate transcript fields: CheckpointTranscriptStart replaces both
   140→	// CondensedTranscriptLines and TranscriptLinesAtStart from older state files.
   141→	if s.CheckpointTranscriptStart == 0 {
   142→		if s.CondensedTranscriptLines > 0 {
   143→			s.CheckpointTranscriptStart = s.CondensedTranscriptLines
   144→		} else if s.TranscriptLinesAtStart > 0 {
   145→			s.CheckpointTranscriptStart = s.TranscriptLinesAtStart
   146→		}
   147→	}
   148→	// Clear deprecated fields so they aren't re-persisted
   149→	s.CondensedTranscriptLines = 0
   150→	s.TranscriptLinesAtStart = 0
   151→}

   153→// StateStore provides low-level operations for managing session state files.
   154→//
   155→// StateStore is a primitive for session state persistence. It is NOT the same as
   156→// the Sessions interface - it only handles state files in .git/entire-sessions/,
   157→// not the full session data which includes checkpoint content.
   158→//
   159→// Use StateStore directly in strategies for performance-critical state operations.
   160→// Use the Sessions interface (when implemented) for high-level session management.
   161→type StateStore struct {
   162→	// stateDir is the directory where session state files are stored
   163→	stateDir string
   164→}
   165→
   166→// NewStateStore creates a new state store.
   167→// Uses the git common dir to store session state (shared across worktrees).
   168→func NewStateStore() (*StateStore, error) {
   169→	commonDir, err := getGitCommonDir()
   170→	if err != nil {
   171→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get git common dir: %w", err)
   172→	}
   173→	return &StateStore{
   174→		stateDir: filepath.Join(commonDir, SessionStateDirName),
   175→	}, nil
   176→}
   177→
   178→// NewStateStoreWithDir creates a new state store with a custom directory.
   179→// This is useful for testing.
   180→func NewStateStoreWithDir(stateDir string) *StateStore {
   181→	return &StateStore{stateDir: stateDir}
   182→}
   183→
   184→// Load loads the session state for the given session ID.
   185→// Returns (nil, nil) when session file doesn't exist (not an error condition).
   186→func (s *StateStore) Load(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) (*State, error) {
   187→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   188→
   189→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   190→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   191→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   192→	}
   193→
   194→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(sessionID)
   195→
   196→	data, err := os.ReadFile(stateFile) //nolint:gosec // stateFile is derived from sessionID
   197→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   198→		return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // nil,nil indicates session not found (expected case)
   199→	}
   200→	if err != nil {
   201→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state: %w", err)
   202→	}
   203→
   204→	var state State
   205→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &state); err != nil {
   206→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal session state: %w", err)
   207→	}
   208→	state.NormalizeAfterLoad()
   209→	return &state, nil
   210→}
   211→
   212→// Save saves the session state atomically.
   213→func (s *StateStore) Save(ctx context.Context, state *State) error {
   214→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   215→
   216→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   217→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(state.SessionID); err != nil {
   218→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   219→	}
   220→
   221→	if err := os.MkdirAll(s.stateDir, 0o750); err != nil {
   222→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session state directory: %w", err)
   223→	}
   224→
   225→	data, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(state, "", "  ")
   226→	if err != nil {
   227→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal session state: %w", err)
   228→	}
   229→
   230→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(state.SessionID)
   231→
   232→	// Atomic write: write to temp file, then rename
   233→	tmpFile := stateFile + ".tmp"
   234→	if err := os.WriteFile(tmpFile, data, 0o600); err != nil {
   235→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write session state: %w", err)
   236→	}
   237→	if err := os.Rename(tmpFile, stateFile); err != nil {
   238→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to rename session state file: %w", err)
   239→	}
   240→	return nil
   241→}
   242→
   243→// Clear removes the session state file for the given session ID.
   244→func (s *StateStore) Clear(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) error {
   245→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   246→
   247→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   248→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   249→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   250→	}
   251→
   252→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(sessionID)
   253→
   254→	if err := os.Remove(stateFile); err != nil {
   255→		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   256→			return nil // Already gone, not an error
   257→		}
   258→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove session state file: %w", err)
   259→	}
   260→	return nil
   261→}
   262→
   263→// RemoveAll removes the entire session state directory.
   264→// This is used during uninstall to completely remove all session state.
   265→func (s *StateStore) RemoveAll() error {
   266→	if err := os.RemoveAll(s.stateDir); err != nil {
   267→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove session state directory: %w", err)
   268→	}
   269→	return nil
   270→}
   271→
   272→// List returns all session states.
   273→func (s *StateStore) List(ctx context.Context) ([]*State, error) {
   274→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   275→
   276→	entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.stateDir)
   277→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   278→		return nil, nil
   279→	}
   280→	if err != nil {
   281→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state directory: %w", err)
   282→	}
   283→
   284→	var states []*State
   285→	for _, entry := range entries {
   286→		if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json") {
   287→			continue
   288→		}
   289→		if strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".tmp") {
   290→			continue // Skip temp files
   291→		}
   292→
   293→		sessionID := strings.TrimSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json")
   294→		state, err := s.Load(ctx, sessionID)
   295→		if err != nil {
   296→			continue // Skip corrupted state files
   297→		}
   298→		if state == nil {
   299→			continue
   300→		}
   301→
   302→		states = append(states, state)
   303→	}
   304→	return states, nil
   305→}
   306→
   307→// stateFilePath returns the path to a session state file.
   308→func (s *StateStore) stateFilePath(sessionID string) string {
   309→	return filepath.Join(s.stateDir, sessionID+".json")
   310→}
   311→
   312→// getGitCommonDir returns the path to the shared git directory.
   313→// In a regular checkout, this is .git/
   314→// In a worktree, this is the main repo's .git/ (not .git/worktrees/<name>/)
   315→func getGitCommonDir() (string, error) {
   316→	ctx := context.Background()
   317→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
   318→	cmd.Dir = "."
   319→	output, err := cmd.Output()
   320→	if err != nil {
   321→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get git common dir: %w", err)
   322→	}
   323→
   324→	commonDir := strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
   325→
   326→	// git rev-parse --git-common-dir returns relative paths from the working directory,
   327→	// so we need to make it absolute if it isn't already
   328→	if !filepath.IsAbs(commonDir) {
   329→		commonDir = filepath.Join(".", commonDir)
   330→	}
   331→
   332→	return filepath.Clean(commonDir), nil
   333→}

Now I understand the test patterns. The tests for PostCommit are more like integration tests since PostCommit calls many internal methods (condense, shadow branch operations, etc.). For unit-level TDD, I need to focus on what's new: the phase transition logic and conditional action dispatch.

The key insight is that PostCommit's core logic change is:
1. Before phase transition: always condenses sessions with new content, always deletes shadow branch
2. After phase transition: the state machine decides whether to condense, and shadow branch deletion depends on whether any active session remains

Given the complexity of PostCommit (it requires a full git repo with shadow branches), the tests for phase-aware behavior are best structured as tests that:
1. Set up a git repo with a session in a specific phase
2. Create a commit with an Entire-Checkpoint trailer
3. Call PostCommit() and verify the resulting session phase

This is similar to how `phase_wiring_test.go` works for `InitializeSession`. Let me write these tests. I'll dispatch both test-writing tasks in parallel using subagents.

    23→// The shadow branch must be preserved because the session is still active.

   111→// TestPostCommit_RebaseDuringActive_SkipsTransition verifies that PostCommit
   112→// is a no-op during rebase operations, leaving the session phase unchanged.
   113→func TestPostCommit_RebaseDuringActive_SkipsTransition(t *testing.T) {

   172→// TestPostCommit_ShadowBranch_PreservedWhenActiveSessionExists verifies that
   173→// the shadow branch is preserved when ANY session on it is still active,

   233→// setupSessionWithCheckpoint initializes a session and creates one checkpoint
   234→// on the shadow branch so there is content available for condensation.
   235→func setupSessionWithCheckpoint(t *testing.T, s *ManualCommitStrategy, repo *git.Repository, dir, sessionID string) {
   236→	t.Helper()
   237→
   238→	// Create metadata directory with a transcript file
   239→	metadataDir := ".entire/metadata/" + sessionID
   240→	metadataDirAbs := filepath.Join(dir, metadataDir)
   241→	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(metadataDirAbs, 0o755))
   242→
   243→	transcript := `{"type":"human","message":{"content":"test prompt"}}
   244→{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":"test response"}}
   245→`
   246→	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(
   247→		filepath.Join(metadataDirAbs, paths.TranscriptFileName),
   248→		[]byte(transcript), 0o644))
   249→
   250→	// SaveChanges creates the shadow branch and checkpoint
   251→	err := s.SaveChanges(SaveContext{
   252→		SessionID:      sessionID,
   253→		ModifiedFiles:  []string{},
   254→		NewFiles:       []string{},
   255→		DeletedFiles:   []string{},
   256→		MetadataDir:    metadataDir,
   257→		MetadataDirAbs: metadataDirAbs,
   258→		CommitMessage:  "Checkpoint 1",
   259→		AuthorName:     "Test",
   260→		AuthorEmail:    "test@test.com",
   261→	})
   262→	require.NoError(t, err, "SaveChanges should succeed to create shadow branch content")
   263→}
   264→
   265→// commitWithCheckpointTrailer creates a commit on the current branch with the
   266→// Entire-Checkpoint trailer in the commit message. This simulates what happens
   267→// after PrepareCommitMsg adds the trailer and the user completes the commit.
   268→func commitWithCheckpointTrailer(t *testing.T, repo *git.Repository, dir, checkpointIDStr string) {
   269→	t.Helper()
   270→
   271→	cpID := id.MustCheckpointID(checkpointIDStr)
   272→
   273→	// Modify a file so there is something to commit
   274→	testFile := filepath.Join(dir, "test.txt")
   275→	content := "updated at " + time.Now().String()
   276→	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(testFile, []byte(content), 0o644))
   277→
   278→	wt, err := repo.Worktree()
   279→	require.NoError(t, err)
   280→
   281→	_, err = wt.Add("test.txt")
   282→	require.NoError(t, err)
   283→
   284→	commitMsg := "test commit\n\n" + trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ": " + cpID.String() + "\n"
   285→	_, err = wt.Commit(commitMsg, &git.CommitOptions{
   286→		Author: &object.Signature{
   287→			Name:  "Test",
   288→			Email: "test@test.com",
   289→			When:  time.Now(),
   290→		},
   291→	})
   292→	require.NoError(t, err, "commit with checkpoint trailer should succeed")
   293→}

   181→// createTestCheckpoint creates a minimal checkpoint on the shadow branch so that
   182→// the session appears to have content. This writes a test file change and saves
   183→// a checkpoint via the strategy.
   184→func createTestCheckpoint(t *testing.T, repoDir string, s *ManualCommitStrategy, sessionID string) error {
   185→	t.Helper()
   186→
   187→	// Modify a file in the working tree to create "dirty" state
   188→	testFile := filepath.Join(repoDir, "test.txt")
   189→	if err := os.WriteFile(testFile, []byte("modified content"), 0o644); err != nil {
   190→		return err
   191→	}
   192→
   193→	// Stage the change so it appears in git status
   194→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(repoDir)
   195→	if err != nil {
   196→		return err
   197→	}
   198→	wt, err := repo.Worktree()
   199→	if err != nil {
   200→		return err
   201→	}
   202→	if _, err := wt.Add("test.txt"); err != nil {
   203→		return err
   204→	}
   205→
   206→	// Use SaveChanges to create a real checkpoint on the shadow branch
   207→	ctx := SaveContext{
   208→		SessionID:      sessionID,
   209→		AgentType:      "Claude Code",
   210→		Transcript:     []byte(`{"type":"message","role":"assistant"}`),
   211→		TranscriptPath: "",
   212→	}
   213→	return s.SaveChanges(ctx)
   214→}

In the action loop, ActionMigrateShadowBranch is dispatched. No condensation happens, so `condensed = false`. Then `updateBaseCommitIfChanged` runs. 1. **Amend (`source="commit"`)**: Remove `"commit"` from the early-return switch. Instead, handle it specially: if message already has trailer → keep. If any session has `PendingCheckpointID` → restore. Otherwise, no-op.

2. **Normal commits**: If any session has `PendingCheckpointID` → use it instead of generating new one.

3. **New content with no pending ID**: Generate new ID and store it as `PendingCheckpointID`.

    53→	}
    54→	return CheckpointID(hex.EncodeToString(bytes)), nil
    55→}
    56→
    57→// Validate checks if a string is a valid checkpoint ID format.
    58→// Returns an error if invalid, nil if valid.
    59→func Validate(s string) error {
    60→	if !checkpointIDRegex.MatchString(s) {
    61→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid checkpoint ID %q: must be 12 lowercase hex characters", s)
    62→	}
    63→	return nil
    64→}
    65→
    66→// String returns the checkpoint ID as a string.
    67→func (id CheckpointID) String() string {
    68→	return string(id)
    69→}
    70→
    71→// IsEmpty returns true if the checkpoint ID is empty or unset.
    72→func (id CheckpointID) IsEmpty() bool {
    73→	return id == EmptyCheckpointID
    74→}
    75→
    76→// Path returns the sharded path for this checkpoint ID on entire/sessions.
    77→// Uses first 2 characters as shard (256 buckets), remaining as folder name.
    78→// Example: "a3b2c4d5e6f7" -> "a3/b2c4d5e6f7"
    79→func (id CheckpointID) Path() string {
    80→	if len(id) < 3 {
    81→		return string(id)
    82→	}
    83→	return string(id[:2]) + "/" + string(id[2:])
    84→}
    85→
    86→// MarshalJSON implements json.Marshaler.
    87→func (id CheckpointID) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
    88→	data, err := json.Marshal(string(id))
    89→	if err != nil {
    90→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal checkpoint ID: %w", err)
    91→	}
    92→	return data, nil
    93→}
    94→
    95→// UnmarshalJSON implements json.Unmarshaler with validation.
    96→// Returns an error if the JSON string is not a valid 12-character hex ID.
    97→// Empty strings are allowed and result in EmptyCheckpointID.
    98→func (id *CheckpointID) UnmarshalJSON(data []byte) error {
    99→	var s string
   100→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &s); err != nil {
   101→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal checkpoint ID: %w", err)
   102→	}
   103→	// Allow empty strings (represents unset checkpoint ID)
   104→	if s == "" {
   105→		*id = EmptyCheckpointID
   106→		return nil
   107→	}
   108→	if err := Validate(s); err != nil {
   109→		return err
   110→	}
   111→	*id = CheckpointID(s)
   112→	return nil
   113→}

   218→// TestShadowStrategy_LastCheckpointID_IgnoresOldSessions tests that when multiple
   219→// old sessions exist in the worktree, only the current session (matching BaseCommit)
   220→// is used for checkpoint ID reuse.
   221→//
   222→// This reproduces the bug where old session states from previous days would cause
   223→// different checkpoint IDs to be used when making multiple commits from a new session.
   224→func TestShadowStrategy_LastCheckpointID_IgnoresOldSessions(t *testing.T) {
   225→	t.Parallel()
   226→
   227→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, strategy.StrategyNameManualCommit)
   228→
   229→	// === Create an OLD session on the initial commit ===
   230→	oldSession := env.NewSession()
   231→	if err := env.SimulateUserPromptSubmit(oldSession.ID); err != nil {
   232→		t.Fatalf("SimulateUserPromptSubmit (old session) failed: %v", err)
   233→	}
   234→
   235→	// Old session modifies a file
   236→	env.WriteFile("old.txt", "old session content")
   237→	oldSession.CreateTranscript("Create old file", []FileChange{
   238→		{Path: "old.txt", Content: "old session content"},
   239→	})
   240→
   241→	if err := env.SimulateStop(oldSession.ID, oldSession.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
   242→		t.Fatalf("SimulateStop (old session) failed: %v", err)
   243→	}
   244→
   245→	// Commit from old session
   246→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Old session commit", "old.txt")
   247→	oldCheckpointID := env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(env.GetHeadHash())
   248→	if oldCheckpointID == "" {
   249→		t.Fatal("Old session commit should have checkpoint ID")
   250→	}
   251→	t.Logf("Old session checkpoint ID: %s", oldCheckpointID)
   252→
   253→	// Make an intermediate commit (moves HEAD forward, creates new base for new session)
   254→	env.WriteFile("intermediate.txt", "unrelated change")
   255→	env.GitAdd("intermediate.txt")
   256→	env.GitCommit("Intermediate commit (no session)")
   257→
   258→	// === Create a NEW session on the new HEAD ===
   259→	newSession := env.NewSession()
   260→	if err := env.SimulateUserPromptSubmit(newSession.ID); err != nil {
   261→		t.Fatalf("SimulateUserPromptSubmit (new session) failed: %v", err)
   262→	}
   263→
   264→	// New session modifies two files
   265→	env.WriteFile("fileA.txt", "new session file A")
   266→	env.WriteFile("fileB.txt", "new session file B")
   267→	newSession.CreateTranscript("Create new files A and B", []FileChange{
   268→		{Path: "fileA.txt", Content: "new session file A"},
   269→		{Path: "fileB.txt", Content: "new session file B"},
   270→	})
   271→
   272→	if err := env.SimulateStop(newSession.ID, newSession.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
   273→		t.Fatalf("SimulateStop (new session) failed: %v", err)
   274→	}
   275→
   276→	// At this point, we have TWO session state files:
   277→	// - Old session: BaseCommit = old HEAD, LastCheckpointID = oldCheckpointID
   278→	// - New session: BaseCommit = current HEAD, FilesTouched = ["fileA.txt", "fileB.txt"]
   279→
   280→	// First commit from new session
   281→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add file A from new session", "fileA.txt")
   282→	firstCheckpointID := env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(env.GetHeadHash())
   283→	if firstCheckpointID == "" {
   284→		t.Fatal("First commit should have checkpoint ID")
   285→	}
   286→	t.Logf("First new session checkpoint ID: %s", firstCheckpointID)
   287→
   288→	// CRITICAL: First checkpoint should NOT be the old session's checkpoint
   289→	if firstCheckpointID == oldCheckpointID {
   290→		t.Errorf("First new session commit reused old session checkpoint ID %s (should generate new ID)",
   291→			oldCheckpointID)
   292→	}
   293→
   294→	// Second commit from new session
   295→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add file B from new session", "fileB.txt")
   296→	secondCheckpointID := env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(env.GetHeadHash())
   297→	if secondCheckpointID == "" {
   298→		t.Fatal("Second commit should have checkpoint ID")
   299→	}
   300→	t.Logf("Second new session checkpoint ID: %s", secondCheckpointID)
   301→
   302→	// CRITICAL: Both commits from new session should have SAME checkpoint ID
   303→	if firstCheckpointID != secondCheckpointID {
   304→		t.Errorf("New session commits should have same checkpoint ID:\n  First:  %s\n  Second: %s",
   305→			firstCheckpointID, secondCheckpointID)
   306→	}
   307→
   308→	// CRITICAL: Neither should be the old session's checkpoint ID
   309→	if secondCheckpointID == oldCheckpointID {
   310→		t.Errorf("Second new session commit reused old session checkpoint ID %s",
   311→			oldCheckpointID)
   312→	}
   313→}

> AGENT

I understand the issue. The `REDACTED` test at line 110 tests:

1. Session creates work → Stop → Commit (generates checkpoint ID, sets `LastCheckpointID`)
2. User enters new prompt (should clear `LastCheckpointID`)
3. Session creates more work → Stop → Commit
4. **Expects**: second checkpoint ID is different from first

The problem is that after condensation in step 1, `PendingCheckpointID` is set (by my PostCommit implementation). Then in step 3, when the second commit happens, `PrepareCommitMsg` finds `PendingCheckpointID` set on the session and reuses it, even though a new prompt was entered.

The fix: `PendingCheckpointID` needs to be cleared when a new prompt starts (when `user-prompt-submit` fires). Let me look at how the `user-prompt-submit` hook works — it calls `InitializeSession` or similar.

Let me check what `SimulateUserPromptSubmit` does and how the session state gets updated on new prompts.

`ApplyCommonActions` doesn't clear `PendingCheckpointID`. The `InitializeSession` flow calls `session.Transition(state.Phase, session.EventTurnStart, ...)` and `session.ApplyCommonActions()`. But neither clears `PendingCheckpointID`.

Looking at the test flow:
1. First commit → PostCommit sets `PendingCheckpointID` during condensation
2. `SimulateUserPromptSubmit` → calls `InitializeSession` → transitions phase but doesn't clear `PendingCheckpointID`
3. Second commit → PrepareCommitMsg finds `PendingCheckpointID` and reuses it (BUG)

The fix should be to clear `PendingCheckpointID` when a new turn starts (EventTurnStart). This is conceptually correct: when a new prompt arrives, any pending checkpoint from a previous commit cycle should be cleared because the new work should get a fresh checkpoint ID.

The cleanest place to clear it is in `ApplyCommonActions` when `ActionUpdateLastInteraction` fires (which happens on every turn start). But that would couple the session package to the `PendingCheckpointID` concept, which is strategy-specific.

Actually, looking more carefully at where `PendingCheckpointID` is defined — it's on `session.State` itself (line 51-53 in `session/state.go`), so it's already part of the session package. The most natural fix is to clear it in `InitializeSession` when a new turn starts.

I understand the issue now. The test flow:

1. Session starts, two prompts, Stop → checkpoint on shadow branch
2. First commit → PostCommit condensation → sets `PendingCheckpointID` (my change)  
3. Continue session (no `SimulateUserPromptSubmit`) → third prompt → Stop → new checkpoint
4. Second commit → PrepareCommitMsg finds `PendingCheckpointID` → **reuses it** (WRONG — should generate new ID because there's NEW content to condense)

The problem is that `PendingCheckpointID` should be reused for the **same content** (e.g., amend), but when there's NEW content since the last condensation, a new ID should be generated.

Looking at the logic more carefully: `PendingCheckpointID` is meant for the amend case (restoring a trailer that was lost). For normal commits with new content, it should only be reused if there's NO new content beyond what was already condensed. But in this case, there IS new content (the third prompt created a new checkpoint on the shadow branch).

The fix: I need to reconsider when to reuse `PendingCheckpointID`. It should be used:
- **For amend** (`source="commit"`): always (this is the main use case)
- **For normal commits** with new content: only if it's the same content (i.e., the `PendingCheckpointID` was set and no new checkpoints were added after it)

Actually, thinking about it more carefully, the simplest correct approach is:
- `PendingCheckpointID` should be cleared when new content is saved (i.e., when `SaveChanges`/`SaveTaskCheckpoint` creates a new checkpoint on the shadow branch), because new content means a new checkpoint cycle.
- It should also be cleared on `InitializeSession` (new prompt).

But `PendingCheckpointID` is set by PostCommit (during condensation), and new content arrives via `SimulateStop` → `SaveChanges`. The flow in the failing test:

1. SaveChanges (checkpoint 1) → PendingCheckpointID empty
2. Commit → PostCommit sets PendingCheckpointID  
3. SaveChanges (checkpoint 2 — new content!) → PendingCheckpointID should be cleared here
4. Commit → PrepareCommitMsg should generate new ID

So the fix is to clear `PendingCheckpointID` in `SaveChanges` when a new checkpoint is created. Let me find where `SaveChanges` updates state.

All tasks are complete. Here's a summary of what was implemented:

**Batch complete — Tasks 5 & 6 for PR 3:**

### What was implemented:

**Task 5: Phase-Aware PostCommit** (`manual_commit_hooks.go`)
- Rewrote `PostCommit()` to use the session state machine: each session goes through `session.Transition(EventGitCommit)` and dispatches actions
- ACTIVE → ACTIVE_COMMITTED (defers condensation)
- IDLE → condenses immediately 
- ACTIVE_COMMITTED → migrates shadow branch
- ENDED → condenses if files touched, discards if empty
- Rebase detection: skips all transitions during rebase/cherry-pick/revert
- Shadow branches only deleted when ALL sessions on the branch are non-active
- Sets `PendingCheckpointID` on condensed sessions for amend trailer restoration

**Task 6: PrepareCommitMsg Amend Fix** (`manual_commit_hooks.go`)
- Removed `"commit"` from early-return switch (was the root cause of the amend bug)
- Added `handleAmendCommitMsg()` method for `source="commit"`: preserves existing trailer or restores from `PendingCheckpointID`
- Normal commits now check `PendingCheckpointID` before generating new IDs (idempotent checkpoint IDs)
- Clears `PendingCheckpointID` on new prompt start (`InitializeSession`) and on new checkpoint save (`SaveChanges`)

**Tests added:**
- 4 PostCommit tests in `phase_postcommit_test.go`
- 4 PrepareCommitMsg tests in `phase_prepare_commit_msg_test.go`

**Verification:** `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci` — all clean.

Ready for feedback.

---

## Code Review: Phase-Aware Git Hooks (Tasks 5-6, ENT-221)

### What Was Done Well

The implementation is well-structured and closely follows the plan. The refactoring of `PostCommit()` from a monolithic condense-all approach to a per-session state machine dispatch is clean and maintainable. The extraction of `condenseAndUpdateState()` and `updateBaseCommitIfChanged()` as helper methods reduces complexity in the main loop. The test coverage targets the critical scenarios (ACTIVE deferral, IDLE condensation, rebase skip, multi-session shadow branch preservation). All tests pass, and lint/fmt are clean.

The `PendingCheckpointID` lifecycle is well-reasoned -- set during condensation, cleared on new prompt (InitializeSession) and new checkpoint (SaveChanges), restored during amend. The `handleAmendCommitMsg()` is a focused, self-contained method.

---

### Plan Alignment

**Task 5 (PostCommit):** The implementation closely matches the plan's pseudocode (lines 464-494). All four phase-based paths are handled: ACTIVE defers, IDLE condenses, ACTIVE_COMMITTED migrates, ENDED condenses-if-files/discards-if-empty. The shadow branch deletion logic matches the "check all sessions" design (lines 486-494). Rebase detection skips all transitions as specified.

**Task 6 (PrepareCommitMsg Amend Fix):** The implementation matches the plan's logic (lines 513-534). The `"commit"` case was removed from the early-return switch, `handleAmendCommitMsg()` was added, and normal commits now check `PendingCheckpointID` before generating new IDs.

**Deviation from plan:** The plan (line 461) says to modify `manual_commit_migration.go`, but no changes were made to that file. This appears intentional -- `migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded` is called unchanged from PostCommit and works correctly in the new dispatch context. No issue here.

---

### Issues

#### Important (should fix)

**1. Stale doc comment on `PrepareCommitMsg` (line 186)**

The function's doc comment at `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/3/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go` line 186 still says:

```
//   - "merge", "squash", "commit": skip trailer entirely (auto-generated or amend commits)
```

This is now incorrect -- `"commit"` (amend) is no longer skipped; it is handled by `handleAmendCommitMsg()`. The comment should be updated to reflect the new behavior:

```
//   - "merge", "squash": skip trailer entirely (auto-generated messages)
//   - "commit": amend operation - preserves existing trailer or restores from PendingCheckpointID
```

**2. `ActionDiscardIfNoFiles` does not actually discard anything**

In `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/3/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go` lines 587-592:

```go
case session.ActionDiscardIfNoFiles:
    if len(state.FilesTouched) == 0 {
        logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: discarding empty ended session",
            slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
        )
    }
```

This logs "discarding" but performs no actual cleanup -- no session state file removal, no phase change, nothing. The session state is saved after the loop with whatever phase the transition result set (PhaseEnded per the state machine). The plan says (line 479): `if len(state.FilesTouched) == 0 { discard(state) }`. 

This is likely intentional deferral -- "discard" might mean "just don't condense, let it age" rather than "delete state file now." But the log message saying "discarding" is misleading when nothing is discarded. Either:
- Add actual cleanup (e.g., `s.clearSessionState(state.SessionID)`), or
- Change the log message to something like "skipping empty ended session (no files to condense)" to avoid confusion.

**3. Redundant `hasNew` guard on `ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched` (line 582)**

```go
case session.ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched:
    if len(state.FilesTouched) > 0 && hasNew {
```

The state machine already only emits `ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched` when `ctx.HasFilesTouched` is true (see `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/3/cmd/entire/cli/session/phase.go` lines 269-273 -- the `if ctx.HasFilesTouched` guard is in the transition function). So the `len(state.FilesTouched) > 0` check here is redundant with what the state machine already decided. However, the `hasNew` check (transcript has new content beyond what was condensed) is a valid additional guard. 

This is not a bug, but the redundant `FilesTouched` check makes the code harder to reason about -- a reader might wonder "who is the source of truth, the state machine or the dispatch code?" Consider adding a brief comment explaining that `hasNew` is an additional content-level check beyond the state machine's phase-level decision.

#### Suggestions (nice to have)

**4. Blank line between doc comment and function signature on `handleAmendCommitMsg`**

At `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/3/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go` lines 411-415:

```go
// handleAmendCommitMsg handles the prepare-commit-msg hook for amend operations
// (source="commit"). It preserves existing trailers or restores from PendingCheckpointID.
//

func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) handleAmendCommitMsg(logCtx context.Context, commitMsgFile string) error {
```

There is a trailing `//` on line 413 and a blank line on line 414 between the doc comment and the function. While this does not affect functionality or lint, it is an unusual style. Standard Go convention has the doc comment immediately above the function with no blank lines. This is minor but worth tidying.

**5. Missing blank line between `handleAmendCommitMsg` dispatch and the `repo, err := OpenRepository()` call (line 216-217)**

```go
	if source == "commit" {
		return s.handleAmendCommitMsg(logCtx, commitMsgFile)
	}
	repo, err := OpenRepository()
```

This is fine syntactically but the lack of a blank line between the amend dispatch and the start of normal-commit logic makes the flow slightly harder to scan. A blank line after the amend block would improve readability.

**6. Test comment inaccuracies in `phase_prepare_commit_msg_test.go`**

In `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/3/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/phase_prepare_commit_msg_test.go`:

- Lines 25-28 (`TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendPreservesExistingTrailer`): The comment says "This currently FAILS because PrepareCommitMsg returns early for source='commit' before checking the existing message." Since the fix is now implemented, this comment is stale. It should be updated to describe the current (fixed) behavior.

- Lines 62-64 (`TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendRestoresTrailerFromPendingCheckpointID`): Same issue -- says "This FAILS because PrepareCommitMsg currently returns early for source='commit'" which is no longer true.

- Lines 148-150 (`TestPrepareCommitMsg_NormalCommitUsesPendingCheckpointID`): Says "This FAILS because the current code always generates a new ID" which is also no longer true.

These "currently FAILS" comments were presumably written before the fix was implemented (test-first approach) but should be cleaned up before merge.

**7. Consider testing the ENDED phase path in PostCommit**

The four PostCommit tests cover ACTIVE, IDLE, rebase, and multi-session shadow branch preservation. There is no test for the ENDED phase path (condense-if-files-touched / discard-if-no-files). Given that `ActionDiscardIfNoFiles` is a no-op (issue #2 above), a test for ENDED with files vs. ENDED without files would help verify the intended behavior and catch future regressions.

**8. `hasNew` variable shadows error semantics on content check failure**

In `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/3/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go` lines 554-561:

```go
hasNew, contentErr := s.sessionHasNewContent(repo, state)
if contentErr != nil {
    logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: error checking session content",
        slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
        slog.String("error", contentErr.Error()),
    )
}
```

When `contentErr != nil`, `hasNew` is `false`, meaning the session will be treated as having no new content. The old code in `filterSessionsWithNewContent` (line 714) did the opposite -- on error it included the session (fail-open). This is a behavior change from the previous implementation. For hooks that "must be silent on failure," fail-open is generally safer (it's better to condense data that might not need it than to silently skip data that should have been condensed). Consider whether this should be `hasNew = true` on error, or at minimum document the design choice.

---

### Summary

The implementation is solid and well-aligned with the plan. The state machine dispatch in PostCommit is clean and the amend fix addresses a real bug correctly. The `PendingCheckpointID` lifecycle is sound.

The most actionable items are:
1. **Important:** Update the stale doc comment on `PrepareCommitMsg` (line 186).
2. **Important:** Decide on actual behavior for `ActionDiscardIfNoFiles` -- either add real cleanup or fix the misleading log message.
3. **Important:** The fail-open vs fail-closed change in content error handling (issue #8) is a subtle behavior change worth considering.
4. **Suggestion:** Clean up the stale "This currently FAILS" test comments.

### Review Summary

### Issues Addressed from First Review

#### 1. **Doc Comment on PrepareCommitMsg** ✓ FIXED
**Location:** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:183-188`

**Original Issue:** Stale comment incorrectly listed `source="commit"` with "merge" and "squash" as "skip trailer entirely"

**Fix Applied:**
```go
// Before (misleading):
//   - "merge", "squash", "commit": skip trailer entirely (auto-generated or amend commits)

// After (accurate):
//   - "merge", "squash": skip trailer entirely (auto-generated messages)
//   - "commit": amend operation - preserves existing trailer or restores from PendingCheckpointID
```

**Assessment:** Correct. The comment now accurately describes that amend is handled separately via `handleAmendCommitMsg()`, which preserves or restores trailers instead of skipping them.

---

#### 2. **Misleading "Discarding" Log Message** ✓ FIXED
**Location:** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:593-597`

**Original Issue:** `ActionDiscardIfNoFiles` logged "discarding empty session" but didn't actually discard anything

**Fix Applied:**
```go
// Before:
logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: discarding empty ended session")

// After:
logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: skipping empty ended session (no files to condense)",
    slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
)
```

**Assessment:** Excellent fix. The message now accurately describes the behavior (skipping condensation) rather than implying deletion. The added `session_id` attribute also improves debuggability.

---

#### 3. **Fail-Open vs Fail-Closed Inconsistency** ✓ FIXED
**Location:** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:554-564`

**Original Issue:** Content check error set `hasNew = false`, conflicting with prior behavior and the fail-open comment

**Fix Applied:**
```go
// Before:
hasNew, contentErr := s.sessionHasNewContent(repo, state)
if contentErr != nil {
    hasNew = false  // BUG: inconsistent with comment
    logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: error checking session content, skipping condensation")
}

// After:
hasNew, contentErr := s.sessionHasNewContent(repo, state)
if contentErr != nil {
    hasNew = true  // Consistent with fail-open policy
    logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: error checking session content, assuming new content",
        slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
        slog.String("error", contentErr.Error()),
    )
}
```

**Assessment:** Correct fix. This preserves the conservative fail-open behavior (prefer condensing over silently losing data). The improved log message clearly explains the assumption and includes error details for debugging.

---

#### 4. **Stale Test Comments Removed** ✓ FIXED
**Location:** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/phase_prepare_commit_msg_test.go`

**Original Issue:** Comments like "This FAILS due to the bug" and "This will FAIL" were left in after bug fix

**Fix Applied:** All stale failure comments removed from test file. Tests now document expected behavior without referencing past bugs.

**Assessment:** Clean. The tests now serve as clear specifications of correct behavior.

---

#### 7. **Clarifying Comment on Redundant Check** ✓ FIXED
**Location:** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:584-591`

**Original Issue:** `ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched` appeared redundant since state machine already checks `HasFilesTouched`

**Fix Applied:**
```go
case session.ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched:
    // The state machine already gates this action on HasFilesTouched,
    // but hasNew is an additional content-level check (transcript has
    // new content beyond what was previously condensed).
    if len(state.FilesTouched) > 0 && hasNew {
        if s.condenseAndUpdateState(...) {
            condensed = true
        }
    }
```

**Assessment:** Excellent clarification. This explains the two-level gating: state machine checks for files touched (user made changes), and the local `hasNew` check ensures there's actual transcript content to condense. Both checks are necessary.

Confirmed: `migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded` at line 67 **removes the old reference**. If an ACTIVE_COMMITTED session migrates first, the old shadow branch ref is gone, and a subsequent IDLE session's `CondenseSession` will fail with "shadow branch not found".

This is a valid bug. The fix is to process condensation actions before migration actions. The simplest approach: do two passes — first process all condensations (IDLE/ENDED), then process migrations (ACTIVE_COMMITTED).

> AGENT

The shadow branch is still not being found. The IDLE session condensed fine (line 238 assertion would have caught it), but the shadow branch reference at the NEW hash isn't found. Let me think about this...

The issue: with two-pass, the ACTIVE session's migration is now in pass 2. But the ACTIVE session's `updateBaseCommitIfChanged` (line 613) already updated `state.BaseCommit` to the new HEAD in pass 1 (since it wasn't condensed). Then the test at line 230 uses `activeState.BaseCommit` (the new HEAD) to compute the shadow branch name. But the migration (which actually creates the new ref) hasn't run yet... wait, it HAS run in pass 2 now. Let me re-read the flow.

Actually the issue is: the ACTIVE session's state was saved in pass 1 (line 617) with the updated BaseCommit, but migration runs in pass 2 and saves again. However, in pass 1 `updateBaseCommitIfChanged` updates `state.BaseCommit` but migration hasn't renamed the branch yet. Then pass 2 calls `migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded`, which checks if `state.BaseCommit != currentHead`... but `state.BaseCommit` was already updated to `currentHead` by `updateBaseCommitIfChanged` in pass 1! So migration thinks no migration is needed.

The fix: for sessions with `ActionMigrateShadowBranch`, I should NOT run `updateBaseCommitIfChanged` in pass 1. The migration in pass 2 will handle the BaseCommit update.

"TestPrepareCommitMsg_NormalCommitUsesPendingCheckpointID sets PendingCheckpointID + StepCount and creates shadow-branch content via low-level plumbing, but ManualCommitStrategy.SaveChanges clears PendingCheckpointID whenever it writes new content to the shadow branch. That means this state combination may be unrepresentative of real execution (and could pass even if the intended PendingCheckpointID reuse path never occurs). Consider building the scenario via the real SaveChanges/PostCommit lifecycle (or adjust expectations) so the test matches production state transitions.\n```suggestion\n\t// Set the session to ACTIVE_COMMITTED with a PendingCheckpointID\n\tstate, err := s.loadSessionState(sessionID)\n\trequire.NoError(t, err)\n\trequire.NotNil(t, state)\n\tstate.Phase = session.PhaseActiveCommitted\n\tstate.PendingCheckpointID = \"fedcba987654\"\n```"

The test uses \\`createShadowBranchWithTranscript\\` to simulate the shadow branch content from step 1 without going through \\`SaveChanges\\` (which would clear \\`PendingCheckpointID\\`). This is deliberate — we're testing step 3's behavior, so we set up the state as it would be after step 2.\n\nThe suggested code change removes \\`StepCount = 1\\`, which is needed because \\`filterSessionsWithNewContent\\` checks whether the shadow branch has commits beyond what's already condensed.\"",

   663→## Edge Cases: External Git Operations
   664→
   665→### `entire reset` while session is ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED
   666→
   667→Warn and require `--force`. If forced: shadow branch deleted, state cleared. Agent
   668→self-heals on next SaveChanges (creates new shadow branch, fresh state). Produces split
   669→data — document that users should wait for session to finish or run `entire sessions fix`.
   670→
   671→### `git stash` while IDLE
   672→
   673→HEAD unchanged, no hooks fire. Shadow branch + session state untouched. `git stash pop`
   674→restores files. **Safe.**
   675→
   676→### `git reset --hard` (to HEAD) while IDLE
   677→
   678→Cleans working directory, HEAD unchanged. Agent's changes gone from working directory but
   679→**preserved on shadow branch**. User can `entire rewind` to restore. **Safe.**
   680→
   681→### `git reset --hard <older-commit>` while IDLE
   682→
   683→HEAD moves backward, no hooks fire. On next `UserPromptSubmit` →
   684→`migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded()` renames shadow branch. **Collision risk** if older commit
   685→already has a shadow branch (pre-existing issue, out of scope).
   686→
   687→### `git rebase` while ACTIVE
   688→
   689→PostCommit detects `.git/rebase-merge/` or `.git/rebase-apply/` and **skips entirely**.
   690→No phase transitions, no shadow branch migration. After rebase completes, next
   691→UserPromptSubmit or Stop handles the HEAD change via normal migration. **Safe.**
   692→
   693→### `git commit --amend`
   694→
   695→PrepareCommitMsg restores `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer from `PendingCheckpointID` in
   696→session state, even if `-m` flag stripped the original trailer. PostCommit defers for
   697→ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED sessions as normal. **Fixed (was a known limitation).**
   698→
   699→### User abandons work (git restore) then starts new session
   700→
   701→- Old session's `FilesTouched` still lists files (even though reverted)
   702→- If ENDED + FilesTouched non-empty → condensed with historical data
   703→- If user wants to fully discard → use `entire reset --session <id>`
   704→- New session starts fresh, shares shadow branch, no cross-contamination
   705→

   712→- **`entire/sessions` → `entire/checkpoints/v1` rename**: Account for the branch rename
   713→  in any new code.
   714→- **Auto-commit strategy**: Phase tracking is not prioritized for auto-commit. If naturally
   715→  compatible, include it. Otherwise, leave for future work. Auto-commit has fallen out of
   716→  favor in practice.

    17→// getSessionStateDir returns the path to the session state directory.
    18→// This is stored in the git common dir so it's shared across all worktrees.
    19→func getSessionStateDir() (string, error) {

    21→	if err != nil {
    22→		return "", err
    23→	}
    24→	return filepath.Join(commonDir, session.SessionStateDirName), nil
    25→}

    27→// sessionStateFile returns the path to a session state file.
    28→func sessionStateFile(sessionID string) (string, error) {
    29→	stateDir, err := getSessionStateDir()
    30→	if err != nil {
    31→		return "", err
    32→	}
    33→	return filepath.Join(stateDir, sessionID+".json"), nil
    34→}
    35→
    36→// LoadSessionState loads the session state for the given session ID.
    37→// Returns (nil, nil) when session file doesn't exist (not an error condition).
    38→func LoadSessionState(sessionID string) (*SessionState, error) {
    39→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
    40→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
    41→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
    42→	}
    43→
    44→	stateFile, err := sessionStateFile(sessionID)
    45→	if err != nil {
    46→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get session state file path: %w", err)
    47→	}
    48→
    49→	data, err := os.ReadFile(stateFile) //nolint:gosec // stateFile is derived from sessionID, not user input
    50→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
    51→		return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // nil,nil indicates session not found (expected case)
    52→	}
    53→	if err != nil {
    54→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state: %w", err)
    55→	}
    56→
    57→	var state SessionState
    58→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &state); err != nil {
    59→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal session state: %w", err)
    60→	}
    61→	state.NormalizeAfterLoad()
    62→	return &state, nil
    63→}
    64→
    65→// SaveSessionState saves the session state atomically.
    66→func SaveSessionState(state *SessionState) error {
    67→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
    68→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(state.SessionID); err != nil {
    69→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
    70→	}
    71→
    72→	stateDir, err := getSessionStateDir()
    73→	if err != nil {
    74→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get session state directory: %w", err)
    75→	}
    76→
    77→	if err := os.MkdirAll(stateDir, 0o750); err != nil {
    78→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session state directory: %w", err)
    79→	}
    80→
    81→	data, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(state, "", "  ")
    82→	if err != nil {
    83→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal session state: %w", err)
    84→	}
    85→
    86→	stateFile, err := sessionStateFile(state.SessionID)
    87→	if err != nil {
    88→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get session state file path: %w", err)
    89→	}
    90→
    91→	// Atomic write: write to temp file, then rename
    92→	tmpFile := stateFile + ".tmp"
    93→	if err := os.WriteFile(tmpFile, data, 0o600); err != nil {
    94→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write session state: %w", err)
    95→	}
    96→	if err := os.Rename(tmpFile, stateFile); err != nil {
    97→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to rename session state file: %w", err)
    98→	}
    99→	return nil
   100→}

   119→	}

   136→// NormalizeAfterLoad applies backward-compatible migrations to state loaded from disk.
   137→// Call this after deserializing a State from JSON.
   138→func (s *State) NormalizeAfterLoad() {
   139→	// Migrate transcript fields: CheckpointTranscriptStart replaces both
   140→	// CondensedTranscriptLines and TranscriptLinesAtStart from older state files.
   141→	if s.CheckpointTranscriptStart == 0 {
   142→		if s.CondensedTranscriptLines > 0 {
   143→			s.CheckpointTranscriptStart = s.CondensedTranscriptLines
   144→		} else if s.TranscriptLinesAtStart > 0 {
   145→			s.CheckpointTranscriptStart = s.TranscriptLinesAtStart
   146→		}
   147→	}
   148→	// Clear deprecated fields so they aren't re-persisted
   149→	s.CondensedTranscriptLines = 0
   150→	s.TranscriptLinesAtStart = 0
   151→}
   152→
   153→// StateStore provides low-level operations for managing session state files.
   154→//
   155→// StateStore is a primitive for session state persistence. It is NOT the same as
   156→// the Sessions interface - it only handles state files in .git/entire-sessions/,
   157→// not the full session data which includes checkpoint content.
   158→//
   159→// Use StateStore directly in strategies for performance-critical state operations.
   160→// Use the Sessions interface (when implemented) for high-level session management.
   161→type StateStore struct {
   162→	// stateDir is the directory where session state files are stored
   163→	stateDir string
   164→}
   165→
   166→// NewStateStore creates a new state store.
   167→// Uses the git common dir to store session state (shared across worktrees).
   168→func NewStateStore() (*StateStore, error) {
   169→	commonDir, err := getGitCommonDir()
   170→	if err != nil {
   171→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get git common dir: %w", err)
   172→	}
   173→	return &StateStore{
   174→		stateDir: filepath.Join(commonDir, SessionStateDirName),
   175→	}, nil
   176→}
   177→
   178→// NewStateStoreWithDir creates a new state store with a custom directory.
   179→// This is useful for testing.
   180→func NewStateStoreWithDir(stateDir string) *StateStore {
   181→	return &StateStore{stateDir: stateDir}
   182→}
   183→
   184→// Load loads the session state for the given session ID.
   185→// Returns (nil, nil) when session file doesn't exist (not an error condition).
   186→func (s *StateStore) Load(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) (*State, error) {
   187→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   188→
   189→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   190→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   191→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   192→	}
   193→
   194→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(sessionID)
   195→
   196→	data, err := os.ReadFile(stateFile) //nolint:gosec // stateFile is derived from sessionID
   197→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   198→		return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // nil,nil indicates session not found (expected case)
   199→	}
   200→	if err != nil {
   201→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state: %w", err)
   202→	}
   203→
   204→	var state State
   205→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &state); err != nil {
   206→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal session state: %w", err)
   207→	}
   208→	state.NormalizeAfterLoad()
   209→	return &state, nil
   210→}
   211→
   212→// Save saves the session state atomically.
   213→func (s *StateStore) Save(ctx context.Context, state *State) error {
   214→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   215→
   216→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   217→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(state.SessionID); err != nil {
   218→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   219→	}
   220→
   221→	if err := os.MkdirAll(s.stateDir, 0o750); err != nil {
   222→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session state directory: %w", err)
   223→	}
   224→
   225→	data, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(state, "", "  ")
   226→	if err != nil {
   227→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal session state: %w", err)
   228→	}
   229→
   230→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(state.SessionID)
   231→
   232→	// Atomic write: write to temp file, then rename
   233→	tmpFile := stateFile + ".tmp"
   234→	if err := os.WriteFile(tmpFile, data, 0o600); err != nil {
   235→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write session state: %w", err)
   236→	}
   237→	if err := os.Rename(tmpFile, stateFile); err != nil {
   238→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to rename session state file: %w", err)
   239→	}
   240→	return nil
   241→}
   242→
   243→// Clear removes the session state file for the given session ID.
   244→func (s *StateStore) Clear(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) error {
   245→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   246→
   247→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   248→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   249→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   250→	}
   251→
   252→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(sessionID)
   253→
   254→	if err := os.Remove(stateFile); err != nil {
   255→		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   256→			return nil // Already gone, not an error
   257→		}
   258→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove session state file: %w", err)
   259→	}
   260→	return nil
   261→}
   262→
   263→// RemoveAll removes the entire session state directory.
   264→// This is used during uninstall to completely remove all session state.
   265→func (s *StateStore) RemoveAll() error {
   266→	if err := os.RemoveAll(s.stateDir); err != nil {
   267→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove session state directory: %w", err)
   268→	}
   269→	return nil
   270→}
   271→
   272→// List returns all session states.
   273→func (s *StateStore) List(ctx context.Context) ([]*State, error) {
   274→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   275→
   276→	entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.stateDir)
   277→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   278→		return nil, nil
   279→	}
   280→	if err != nil {
   281→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state directory: %w", err)
   282→	}
   283→
   284→	var states []*State
   285→	for _, entry := range entries {
   286→		if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json") {
   287→			continue
   288→		}
   289→		if strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".tmp") {
   290→			continue // Skip temp files
   291→		}
   292→
   293→		sessionID := strings.TrimSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json")
   294→		state, err := s.Load(ctx, sessionID)
   295→		if err != nil {
   296→			continue // Skip corrupted state files
   297→		}
   298→		if state == nil {
   299→			continue
   300→		}
   301→
   302→		states = append(states, state)
   303→	}
   304→	return states, nil
   305→}
   306→
   307→// stateFilePath returns the path to a session state file.
   308→func (s *StateStore) stateFilePath(sessionID string) string {
   309→	return filepath.Join(s.stateDir, sessionID+".json")
   310→}
   311→
   312→// getGitCommonDir returns the path to the shared git directory.
   313→// In a regular checkout, this is .git/
   314→// In a worktree, this is the main repo's .git/ (not .git/worktrees/<name>/)
   315→func getGitCommonDir() (string, error) {
   316→	ctx := context.Background()
   317→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
   318→	cmd.Dir = "."
   319→	output, err := cmd.Output()
   320→	if err != nil {
   321→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get git common dir: %w", err)
   322→	}
   323→
   324→	commonDir := strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
   325→
   326→	// git rev-parse --git-common-dir returns relative paths from the working directory,
   327→	// so we need to make it absolute if it isn't already
   328→	if !filepath.IsAbs(commonDir) {
   329→		commonDir = filepath.Join(".", commonDir)
   330→	}
   331→
   332→	return filepath.Clean(commonDir), nil
   333→}

     1→package strategy
     2→
     3→import (
     4→	"encoding/json"
     5→	"fmt"
     6→	"os"
     7→	"path/filepath"
     8→
     9→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/jsonutil"
    10→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/session"
    11→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/validation"
    12→)
    13→
    14→// Session state management functions shared across all strategies.
    15→// SessionState is stored in .git/entire-sessions/{session_id}.json
    16→
    17→// getSessionStateDir returns the path to the session state directory.
    18→// This is stored in the git common dir so it's shared across all worktrees.
    19→func getSessionStateDir() (string, error) {
    20→	commonDir, err := GetGitCommonDir()
    21→	if err != nil {
    22→		return "", err
    23→	}
    24→	return filepath.Join(commonDir, session.SessionStateDirName), nil
    25→}
    26→
    27→// sessionStateFile returns the path to a session state file.
    28→func sessionStateFile(sessionID string) (string, error) {
    29→	stateDir, err := getSessionStateDir()
    30→	if err != nil {
    31→		return "", err
    32→	}
    33→	return filepath.Join(stateDir, sessionID+".json"), nil
    34→}
    35→
    36→// LoadSessionState loads the session state for the given session ID.
    37→// Returns (nil, nil) when session file doesn't exist (not an error condition).
    38→func LoadSessionState(sessionID string) (*SessionState, error) {
    39→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
    40→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
    41→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
    42→	}
    43→
    44→	stateFile, err := sessionStateFile(sessionID)
    45→	if err != nil {
    46→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get session state file path: %w", err)
    47→	}
    48→
    49→	data, err := os.ReadFile(stateFile) //nolint:gosec // stateFile is derived from sessionID, not user input
    50→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
    51→		return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // nil,nil indicates session not found (expected case)
    52→	}
    53→	if err != nil {
    54→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state: %w", err)
    55→	}
    56→
    57→	var state SessionState
    58→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &state); err != nil {
    59→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal session state: %w", err)
    60→	}
    61→	state.NormalizeAfterLoad()
    62→	return &state, nil
    63→}
    64→
    65→// SaveSessionState saves the session state atomically.
    66→func SaveSessionState(state *SessionState) error {
    67→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
    68→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(state.SessionID); err != nil {
    69→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
    70→	}
    71→
    72→	stateDir, err := getSessionStateDir()
    73→	if err != nil {
    74→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get session state directory: %w", err)
    75→	}
    76→
    77→	if err := os.MkdirAll(stateDir, 0o750); err != nil {
    78→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session state directory: %w", err)
    79→	}
    80→
    81→	data, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(state, "", "  ")
    82→	if err != nil {
    83→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal session state: %w", err)
    84→	}
    85→
    86→	stateFile, err := sessionStateFile(state.SessionID)
    87→	if err != nil {
    88→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get session state file path: %w", err)
    89→	}
    90→
    91→	// Atomic write: write to temp file, then rename
    92→	tmpFile := stateFile + ".tmp"
    93→	if err := os.WriteFile(tmpFile, data, 0o600); err != nil {
    94→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write session state: %w", err)
    95→	}
    96→	if err := os.Rename(tmpFile, stateFile); err != nil {
    97→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to rename session state file: %w", err)
    98→	}
    99→	return nil
   100→}
   101→
   102→// ClearSessionState removes the session state file for the given session ID.
   103→func ClearSessionState(sessionID string) error {
   104→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   105→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   106→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   107→	}
   108→
   109→	stateFile, err := sessionStateFile(sessionID)
   110→	if err != nil {
   111→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get session state file path: %w", err)
   112→	}
   113→
   114→	if err := os.Remove(stateFile); err != nil {
   115→		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   116→			return nil // Already gone, not an error
   117→		}
   118→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove session state file: %w", err)
   119→	}
   120→	return nil
   121→}

}

    18→// Reset deletes the shadow branch and session state for the current HEAD.

    20→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) Reset() error {
    21→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
    22→	if err != nil {
    23→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to open git repository: %w", err)
    24→	}
    25→
    26→	// Get current HEAD
    27→	head, err := repo.Head()
    28→	if err != nil {
    29→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
    30→	}
    31→
    32→	// Get current worktree ID for shadow branch naming
    33→	worktreePath, err := GetWorktreePath()
    34→	if err != nil {
    35→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree path: %w", err)
    36→	}
    37→	worktreeID, err := paths.GetWorktreeID(worktreePath)
    38→	if err != nil {
    39→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree ID: %w", err)
    40→	}
    41→
    42→	// Get shadow branch name for current HEAD
    43→	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(head.Hash().String(), worktreeID)
    44→
    45→	// Check if shadow branch exists
    46→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
    47→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
    48→	hasShadowBranch := err == nil
    49→
    50→	// Find sessions for this commit
    51→	sessions, err := s.findSessionsForCommit(head.Hash().String())
    52→	if err != nil {
    53→		sessions = nil // Ignore error, treat as no sessions
    54→	}
    55→
    56→	// If nothing to reset, return early
    57→	if !hasShadowBranch && len(sessions) == 0 {
    58→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Nothing to reset for %s\n", shadowBranchName)
    59→		return nil
    60→	}
    61→
    62→	// Clear all sessions for this commit
    63→	clearedSessions := make([]string, 0)
    64→	for _, state := range sessions {
    65→		if err := s.clearSessionState(state.SessionID); err != nil {
    66→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to clear session state for %s: %v\n", state.SessionID, err)
    67→		} else {

    69→		}
    70→	}

    73→	if len(clearedSessions) > 0 {

    83→		}
    84→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Deleted shadow branch %s\n", shadowBranchName)

---

## Summary

### Task 8: `entire sessions fix` command

**New file created:** `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/3/cmd/entire/cli/sessions_fix.go`

This file contains:

- **`newSessionsCmd()`** -- Parent command `entire sessions` that dispatches to subcommands.
- **`newSessionsFixCmd()`** -- The `entire sessions fix` subcommand with a `--force` flag.
- **`runSessionsFix()`** -- Main logic that:
  1. Scans all session states via `strategy.ListSessionStates()`
  2. Opens the git repository to check shadow branch existence
  3. Classifies each session as stuck or healthy via `classifySession()`
  4. For each stuck session, displays diagnostic info and prompts for action (Condense/Discard/Skip)
  5. With `--force`, automatically condenses all fixable sessions (or discards those without shadow branches)
- **`classifySession()`** -- Determines if a session is stuck:
  - `ACTIVE`/`ACTIVE_COMMITTED` with no interaction for over 1 hour (or nil `LastInteractionTime`)
  - `ENDED` with `StepCount > 0` and shadow branch still exists (uncondensed data)
- **`displayStuckSession()`** -- Prints session ID, phase, reason, agent, last interaction time, shadow branch status, checkpoint count, and files touched count.
- **`promptSessionAction()`** -- Uses `NewAccessibleForm()` with huh select to offer Condense/Discard/Skip options.
- **`discardSession()`** -- Clears session state file and deletes shadow branch if no other sessions need it.
- **`canDeleteShadowBranch()`** -- Checks if other sessions reference the same shadow branch.

### Task 8 (continued): `SessionCondenser` interface

**Modified:** `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/3/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/strategy.go`

Added the `SessionCondenser` interface:

```go
type SessionCondenser interface {
    CondenseSessionByID(sessionID string) error
}
```

**Modified:** `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/3/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go`

Implemented `CondenseSessionByID()` on `ManualCommitStrategy`:
1. Loads session state by ID
2. Opens repository
3. Generates a checkpoint ID via `id.Generate()`
4. Checks shadow branch existence -- if missing, just clears state file
5. Calls `s.CondenseSession(repo, checkpointID, state)` for the actual condensation
6. Updates state: resets `StepCount`, sets `Phase` to `IDLE`, saves `LastCheckpointID`
7. Cleans up shadow branch via `cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused()` if no other sessions need it

Also added `cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused()` helper that checks all session states before deleting a shadow branch.

### Task 9: Reset Guards

**Modified:** `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/3/cmd/entire/cli/reset.go`

- Added `--session <id>` flag for per-session reset
- Added active session guard: before bulk reset, checks if any sessions on current HEAD have `ACTIVE` or `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` phase. If found, warns and requires `--force` to proceed.
- `runResetSession()` -- Handles per-session reset: loads state, confirms with user (unless `--force`), then calls `resetter.ResetSession(sessionID)`.
- `hasActiveSessionsOnCurrentHead()` -- Scans session states for active sessions matching current HEAD.

**Modified:** `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/3/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/strategy.go`

Updated `SessionResetter` interface to add:

```go
ResetSession(sessionID string) error
```

**Modified:** `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/3/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_reset.go`

Implemented `ResetSession()` on `ManualCommitStrategy`:
1. Loads session state by ID
2. Clears the session state file
3. Calls `cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused()` to conditionally delete the shadow branch
4. Reports what was cleaned up

### Root command registration

**Modified:** `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/3/cmd/entire/cli/root.go`

Added `cmd.AddCommand(newSessionsCmd())` to register the new sessions parent command.

### Bonus fix

**Modified:** `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/3/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session_state.go`

Fixed a pre-existing `wrapcheck` lint issue in `ListSessionStates()` where the error from `store.List()` was returned unwrapped.

### Design decisions

1. **Staleness threshold is hardcoded at 1 hour** -- kept simple as specified; not configurable via flag or settings.
2. **`--force` on `sessions fix` condenses when possible, discards otherwise** -- if a session has checkpoint data on a shadow branch, it condenses. If the shadow branch is missing, it discards the state file since there's nothing to salvage.
3. **Shadow branch cleanup is shared** -- `cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused()` is used by both `CondenseSessionByID()` and `ResetSession()` to avoid duplicating the "check other sessions" logic.
4. **Active session guard is permissive** -- it only blocks on `ACTIVE`/`ACTIVE_COMMITTED` phases, not `IDLE` or `ENDED`. This prevents accidentally destroying data for sessions where an agent is currently working.

   170→// classifySession determines if a session is stuck and returns diagnostic info.
   171→// Returns nil if the session is healthy.
   172→func classifySession(state *strategy.SessionState, repo *git.Repository, now time.Time) *stuckSession {
   173→	// Determine shadow branch info
   174→	shadowBranch := checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   175→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranch)
   176→	_, refErr := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   177→	hasShadowBranch := refErr == nil
   178→
   179→	phase := session.PhaseFromString(string(state.Phase))
   180→
   181→	switch {
   182→	case phase.IsActive():
   183→		// Active sessions are stuck if no interaction for over the staleness threshold
   184→		isStale := state.LastInteractionTime == nil || now.Sub(*state.LastInteractionTime) > stalenessThreshold
   185→		if !isStale {
   186→			return nil
   187→		}
   188→
   189→		var reason string
   190→		if state.LastInteractionTime != nil {
   191→			reason = fmt.Sprintf("active, last interaction %s ago", now.Sub(*state.LastInteractionTime).Truncate(time.Minute))
   192→		} else {
   193→			reason = "active, no recorded interaction time"
   194→		}
   195→
   196→		return &stuckSession{
   197→			State:             state,
   198→			Reason:            reason,
   199→			ShadowBranch:      shadowBranch,
   200→			HasShadowBranch:   hasShadowBranch,
   201→			CheckpointCount:   state.StepCount,
   202→			FilesTouchedCount: len(state.FilesTouched),
   203→		}
   204→
   205→	case phase == session.PhaseEnded:
   206→		// Ended sessions are stuck if they have uncondensed data
   207→		if state.StepCount <= 0 || !hasShadowBranch {
   208→			return nil
   209→		}
   210→
   211→		return &stuckSession{
   212→			State:             state,
   213→			Reason:            "ended with uncondensed checkpoint data",
   214→			ShadowBranch:      shadowBranch,
   215→			HasShadowBranch:   hasShadowBranch,
   216→			CheckpointCount:   state.StepCount,
   217→			FilesTouchedCount: len(state.FilesTouched),
   218→		}
   219→
   220→	default:
   221→		return nil
   222→	}
   223→}
   224→
   225→// displayStuckSession prints diagnostic info for a stuck session.
   226→func displayStuckSession(cmd *cobra.Command, ss stuckSession) {
   227→	w := cmd.OutOrStdout()
   228→
   229→	fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Session: %s\n", ss.State.SessionID)
   230→	fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Phase:   %s\n", ss.State.Phase)
   231→	fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Reason:  %s\n", ss.Reason)
   232→
   233→	if ss.State.AgentType != "" {
   234→		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Agent:   %s\n", ss.State.AgentType)
   235→	}
   236→
   237→	if ss.State.LastInteractionTime != nil {
   238→		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Last interaction: %s\n", ss.State.LastInteractionTime.Format(time.RFC3339))
   239→	}
   240→
   241→	shadowStatus := "not found"
   242→	if ss.HasShadowBranch {
   243→		shadowStatus = fmt.Sprintf("exists (%s)", ss.ShadowBranch)
   244→	}
   245→	fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Shadow branch: %s\n", shadowStatus)
   246→	fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Checkpoints: %d, Files touched: %d\n", ss.CheckpointCount, ss.FilesTouchedCount)
   247→}
   248→
   249→// promptSessionAction asks the user what to do with a stuck session.
   250→func promptSessionAction(ss stuckSession, canCondense bool) (string, error) {
   251→	var action string
   252→
   253→	options := make([]huh.Option[string], 0, 3)
   254→	if canCondense && ss.HasShadowBranch && ss.CheckpointCount > 0 {
   255→		options = append(options, huh.NewOption("Condense (save to permanent storage)", "condense"))
   256→	}
   257→	options = append(options,
   258→		huh.NewOption("Discard (remove session data)", "discard"),
   259→		huh.NewOption("Skip (leave as-is)", "skip"),
   260→	)
   261→
   262→	form := NewAccessibleForm(
   263→		huh.NewGroup(
   264→			huh.NewSelect[string]().
   265→				Title(fmt.Sprintf("Fix session %s?", ss.State.SessionID)).
   266→				Options(options...).
   267→				Value(&action),
   268→		),
   269→	)
   270→
   271→	if err := form.Run(); err != nil {
   272→		return "", fmt.Errorf("session fix prompt failed: %w", err)
   273→	}
   274→
   275→	return action, nil
   276→}
   277→
   278→// discardSession removes session state and cleans up the shadow branch.
   279→func discardSession(ss stuckSession, repo *git.Repository) error {
   280→	// Clear session state file
   281→	if err := strategy.ClearSessionState(ss.State.SessionID); err != nil {
   282→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to clear session state: %w", err)
   283→	}
   284→
   285→	// Delete shadow branch if it exists and no other sessions need it
   286→	if ss.HasShadowBranch {
   287→		if shouldDelete, err := canDeleteShadowBranch(ss.ShadowBranch, ss.State.SessionID); err != nil {
   288→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: could not check other sessions for shadow branch: %v\n", err)
   289→		} else if shouldDelete {
   290→			refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(ss.ShadowBranch)
   291→			ref, refErr := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   292→			if refErr == nil {
   293→				if err := repo.Storer.RemoveReference(ref.Name()); err != nil {
   294→					return fmt.Errorf("failed to delete shadow branch: %w", err)
   295→				}
   296→			}
   297→		}
   298→	}
   299→
   300→	return nil
   301→}
   302→
   303→// canDeleteShadowBranch checks if a shadow branch can be safely deleted.
   304→// Returns true if no other sessions (besides excludeSessionID) need this branch.
   305→func canDeleteShadowBranch(shadowBranch, excludeSessionID string) (bool, error) {
   306→	states, err := strategy.ListSessionStates()
   307→	if err != nil {
   308→		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to list session states: %w", err)
   309→	}
   310→
   311→	for _, state := range states {
   312→		if state.SessionID == excludeSessionID {
   313→			continue
   314→		}
   315→		otherShadow := checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   316→		if otherShadow == shadowBranch && state.StepCount > 0 {
   317→			return false, nil
   318→		}
   319→	}
   320→
   321→	return true, nil
   322→}
   323→

    16→// TestShadowStrategy_MidSessionCommit_FromTranscript tests that when Claude commits
    17→// mid-session (before Stop has been called), the prepare-commit-msg hook detects
    18→// the new work by checking the live transcript and adds a checkpoint trailer.
    19→//
    20→// This is scenario 2 from ENT-112:
    21→// - User prompts Claude
    22→// - Claude creates files and commits them
    23→// - No Stop has happened yet (no shadow branch)
    24→// - The commit should still get a checkpoint trailer because the transcript shows file modifications
    25→func TestShadowStrategy_MidSessionCommit_FromTranscript(t *testing.T) {
    26→	t.Parallel()
    27→
    28→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, strategy.StrategyNameManualCommit)
    29→
    30→	session := env.NewSession()
    31→
    32→	// Simulate user prompt (initializes session with BaseCommit and TranscriptPath)
    33→	// We need to pass the transcript path so it gets stored in session state
    34→	input := map[string]string{

    36→		"transcript_path": session.TranscriptPath,
    37→	}
    38→	inputJSON, _ := json.Marshal(input)
    39→	cmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "claude-code", "user-prompt-submit")
    40→	cmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
    41→	cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(inputJSON)
    42→	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
    43→		"ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="+env.ClaudeProjectDir,
    44→	)
    45→	if output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
    46→		t.Fatalf("user-prompt-submit failed: %v\nOutput: %s", err, output)
    47→	}
    48→
    49→	// Verify session state has transcript path
    50→	state, err := env.GetSessionState(session.ID)
    51→	if err != nil {
    52→		t.Fatalf("Failed to get session state: %v", err)
    53→	}
    54→	if state == nil {
    55→		t.Fatal("Session state is nil")
    56→	}
    57→	if state.TranscriptPath == "" {
    58→		t.Error("Session state should have TranscriptPath after user-prompt-submit")

    61→

    63→	env.WriteFile("claude_file.txt", "content from Claude")
    64→
    65→	// Create transcript showing Claude created the file (NO Stop called)

    67→		{Path: "claude_file.txt", Content: "content from Claude"},
    68→	})
    69→
    70→	// Verify NO shadow branch exists (Stop hasn't been called)
    71→	shadowBranches := env.ListBranchesWithPrefix("entire/")
    72→	hasShadowBranch := false
    73→	for _, b := range shadowBranches {
    74→		if b != paths.MetadataBranchName {
    75→			hasShadowBranch = true
    76→			break
    77→		}
    78→	}
    79→	if hasShadowBranch {

    81→	}

   334→
   335→	// ========================================
   336→	// Phase 9: Verify Final State
   337→	// ========================================
   338→	t.Log("Phase 9: Verifying final state")
   339→
   340→	// 2 user commits on feature branch
   341→	// Both should be clean (no Entire-* trailers)
   342→	if strings.Contains(commitMsg, "Entire-Session:") || strings.Contains(commitMsg2, "Entire-Session:") {
   343→		t.Error("Commits should NOT have Entire-Session trailer (clean history)")
   344→	}
   345→
   346→	// 2 checkpoint folders in entire/sessions (Already verified above)
   347→
   348→	// Verify all expected files exist in working directory
   349→	expectedFiles := []string{"README.md", "src/auth.go", "src/bcrypt.go", "src/session.go"}
   350→	for _, f := range expectedFiles {
   351→		if !env.FileExists(f) {
   352→			t.Errorf("Expected file %s to exist in final state", f)
   353→		}
   354→	}
   355→
   356→	// Verify shadow branches exist (can be pruned later)
   357→	if !env.BranchExists(expectedShadowBranch) {
   358→		t.Logf("Note: First shadow branch %s may have been cleaned up", expectedShadowBranch)
   359→	}
   360→	if !env.BranchExists(expectedShadowBranch2) {
   361→		t.Logf("Note: Second shadow branch %s may have been cleaned up", expectedShadowBranch2)
   362→	}
   363→
   364→	t.Log("Shadow full workflow test completed successfully!")
   365→}
